name: McCulloch-Pitts neuron
title: A mathematical neuron
summary: McCulloch and Pitts prove that networks of all-or-none threshold neurons are equivalent to formal logic.
impact: Von Neumann used their notation for the EDVAC design, and Kleene built finite automata theory on it.

name: Turing test
title: The question that started it all
summary: Turing swaps "Can machines think?" for the imitation game, in which an interrogator judges typed replies.
impact: It gave AI a shared, testable question that ELIZA, Searle and 2025 language model trials all returned to.

name: Logic Theorist
title: Rules of thumb prove theorems
summary: Newell, Shaw and Simon's program proves 38 of 52 Principia theorems by heuristic search, not enumeration.
impact: Its selective search over symbol lists led to IPL list processing, the General Problem Solver and symbolic AI.

name: Dartmouth workshop
title: Artificial intelligence gets a name
summary: McCarthy, Minsky, Rochester and Shannon name artificial intelligence and gather its founders at Dartmouth.
impact: The name and its conjecture became the banner for AI labs, departments, journals and funding lines.

name: Perceptron
title: The perceptron
summary: Rosenblatt's perceptron learns to classify patterns by adjusting its connection weights from labeled examples.
impact: Learning weights from errors became a running procedure, the principle backpropagation later extended.

name: LISP
title: Programs become data
summary: McCarthy begins LISP at MIT: recursive functions over lists, with programs written as the same lists they process.
impact: It became the main language of US AI research for three decades and the basis of the 1980s Lisp machine industry.

name: Arthur Samuel's checkers program
title: Learning from a game of checkers
summary: Samuel's IBM 701 checkers program improves by tuning its own position-scoring weights through self-play.
impact: Its rule of nudging an estimate toward a later one became temporal-difference learning.

name: Unimate
title: A programmable arm joins the line
summary: Unimation's Unimate, a teach-and-replay hydraulic arm, starts unloading die castings at a GM plant in New Jersey.
impact: It made the reprogrammable arm a product, seeding an industry with 5 million factory robots in use by 2025.

name: DENDRAL expert system
title: Expertise becomes software
summary: DENDRAL proposes and ranks organic molecule structures from a mass spectrum using encoded chemical rules.
impact: Its lesson that knowledge beats general method spawned MYCIN and the 1980s expert systems industry.

name: ELIZA chatbot
title: A conversation with ELIZA
summary: Weizenbaum's ELIZA mimics a Rogerian therapist by matching keywords and reflecting users' own words back.
impact: People read empathy into it, naming the ELIZA effect and turning Weizenbaum into a lifelong AI critic.

name: Shakey the robot
title: Shakey enters the world
summary: SRI begins Shakey, a camera-equipped robot that perceives rooms, plans actions in logic and pushes boxes.
impact: The project left A* search, the STRIPS planner and the Hough line detector, all still in use.

name: Perceptrons (Minsky and Papert)
title: What one layer cannot compute
summary: Minsky and Papert prove one-layer perceptrons with local detectors cannot compute parity or connectedness.
impact: Its theorems, and a guess that many layers were sterile, cast neural nets as a dead end until the 1980s revival.

name: SHRDLU
title: Understanding inside a world of blocks
summary: Terry Winograd's SHRDLU parses typed English, resolves pronouns and moves blocks in a simulated tabletop world.
impact: Lighthill hailed it as exceptional yet doubted it could scale; its pronoun puzzle became the Winograd schema.

name: First AI winter
title: The first AI winter
summary: Lighthill's report to Britain's Science Research Council finds AI's general ambitions have delivered little.
impact: Britain withdrew support from most AI groups, part of a 1974 to 1980 contraction on 2 continents.

name: MYCIN expert system
title: A consultant built from rules
summary: Shortliffe's MYCIN chains 200 if-then rules backward to pick antibiotics and can explain why it asks each question.
impact: Its engine, stripped of medicine, became EMYCIN for other fields, but MYCIN itself never reached a hospital ward.

name: XCON (R1) expert system
title: Expert systems go into production
summary: DEC puts McDermott's R1 (XCON), a 772-rule system, to work configuring VAX-11/780 computer orders.
impact: The expert-system boom's showcase grew to 6,200 rules, half changed yearly, exposing the cost of upkeep.

name: Neocognitron
title: Shift invariance built into the wiring
summary: Fukushima's NHK network alternates learned S-cell and fixed C-cell layers to recognize patterns wherever they sit.
impact: Its shared-weight and pooling layers become the layout that LeNet and AlexNet later train by backpropagation.

name: Hopfield network
title: Memory as an energy landscape
summary: John Hopfield shows a symmetric network of binary units stores memories as stable states it settles into.
impact: It gave recurrent networks a provable energy function and drew physicists into neural network research.

name: Fifth Generation Computer Systems project
title: Japan bets a decade on logic machines
summary: Japan's MITI founds ICOT to build parallel logic-programming machines for knowledge processing over ten years.
impact: It spurred Britain's Alvey and rival programs; its parallel machines met speed goals but never found a market.

name: Backpropagation
title: Learning by backpropagation
summary: Rumelhart, Hinton and Williams show in Nature that backpropagated errors let hidden units learn their own features.
impact: Its two-pass gradient procedure still trains nearly every deployed neural network.

name: Second AI winter
title: The boom meets its balance sheet
summary: Lisp machine makers and expert-system startups slide into loss as a skeptic takes over DARPA's AI funding.
impact: DARPA's AI and robotics budget fell over a third by 1989, and AAAI membership shrank from its 1987 peak of 16,421.

name: Bayesian networks
title: Uncertainty gets a calculus
summary: Judea Pearl's 1988 book makes graphs of local probabilities, updated by passed messages, AI's tool for uncertainty.
impact: Graphical models displace expert-system certainty factors and later drive turbo decoding, spam filters, causal AI.

name: LeNet (convolutional networks)
title: Learned filters read the mail
summary: LeCun's Bell Labs team trains a shared-weight convolutional network end to end on 7,291 real zip code digits.
impact: Learned filters replace hand-built ones; the line reads millions of checks a day by 1998 and leads to AlexNet.

name: Q-learning
title: Learning what an action is worth
summary: Christopher Watkins' Cambridge thesis defines Q-learning, which learns optimal action values without a model.
impact: Off-policy action values become the core of value-based RL, from Q-routing to DQN playing Atari from pixels.

name: TD-Gammon
title: Learning backgammon from its own games
summary: IBM's TD-Gammon learns backgammon from games against itself, then loses just 7 points in 38 games to top players.
impact: Its rollouts overturn expert opening play, and its self-play value network becomes a template DQN and AlphaGo cite.

name: Support vector machines
title: The widest margin wins
summary: Cortes and Vapnik add slack to the maximum-margin kernel classifier, tying LeNet-4 at 1.1% error on NIST digits.
impact: Convex, theory-backed kernel classifiers became machine learning's default tool until deep networks overtook them.

name: Deep Blue vs Kasparov
title: Deep Blue beats Kasparov
summary: IBM's Deep Blue defeats world champion Garry Kasparov 3.5 to 2.5 in a six-game match in New York.
impact: It ended chess as AI's frontier benchmark, pushing the question to language and perception.

name: LSTM
title: Neural networks learn to remember
summary: Hochreiter and Schmidhuber's gated memory cell lets a recurrent network learn across lags of over 1000 steps.
impact: Gated memory powered speech recognition and Google's production translation until the Transformer displaced it.

name: Random forests
title: Strength from uncorrelated trees
summary: Breiman grows unpruned trees on bootstrap samples, each split weighing a few random features, and lets them vote.
impact: A fast, nearly tuning-free default for tabular data, and one of the 25 most-cited papers published since 2000.

name: Neural probabilistic language model
title: Words become learned representations
summary: Bengio's team learns a vector per word while predicting the next word, beating smoothed n-gram models.
impact: Learned embeddings became the basic unit of neural NLP, reused by word2vec and GloVe.

name: DARPA Grand Challenge
title: Driverless across the desert
summary: Stanford's robot Stanley wins DARPA's 132-mile desert race in 6 h 54 min, one of five finishers among 23 starters.
impact: Its veterans staffed Google's self-driving project, and DARPA made prize challenges a standing research tool.

name: Deep belief networks
title: The deep learning revival
summary: Hinton, Osindero and Teh train a deep network one RBM layer at a time, reaching 1.25% error on MNIST digits.
impact: Layer-wise pretraining made deep networks credible again, leading to deep speech recognition by 2012.

name: NVIDIA CUDA
title: GPUs become programmable compute
summary: NVIDIA posts a public beta of its CUDA C compiler and SDK, letting developers program GPUs directly in C.
impact: It made GPUs the practical substrate for deep learning, from AlexNet's 2012 win to the cuDNN library.

name: ImageNet
title: ImageNet changes the dataset
summary: Deng, Fei-Fei and Princeton colleagues release ImageNet: 3.2 million verified images in 5,247 WordNet categories.
impact: Its 1,000-class challenge became computer vision's shared yardstick, where deep learning won in 2012.

name: IBM Watson
title: Watson wins Jeopardy!
summary: IBM's Watson beats Jeopardy! champions Ken Jennings and Brad Rutter, winning $77,147 to $24,000 and $21,600.
impact: It made machine question answering legible to a mass audience, then got oversold into cancer care.

name: AlexNet
title: AlexNet transforms image recognition
summary: Krizhevsky, Sutskever and Hinton's GPU-trained convolutional network wins ImageNet 2012 with 15.3% top-5 error.
impact: An 11-point margin over hand-engineered features turns computer vision toward learned features and GPU training.

name: word2vec
title: Word relationships in vector space
summary: Mikolov's Google team shows two shallow models learn word vectors from 1.6 billion words in under a day.
impact: Free pretrained vectors make embeddings the default first layer of neural NLP until contextual models arrive.

name: Deep Q-network
title: Learning to play from pixels
summary: DeepMind's Q-network learns 7 Atari games from raw pixels with one recipe, beating prior methods on 6.
impact: Deep reinforcement learning becomes a research program, as Double DQN, A3C and Rainbow refine its recipe.

name: Variational autoencoder
title: Learning a generative latent space
summary: Kingma and Welling backpropagate through random sampling to train a generative autoencoder.
impact: It becomes a standard generative component, from beta-VAE and VQ-VAE to Stable Diffusion's latent space.

name: Generative adversarial networks
title: Machines learn to imagine
summary: Goodfellow's Montreal team trains a generator by pitting it against a discriminator network.
impact: GANs carry image synthesis to photoreal StyleGAN faces by 2018, before diffusion overtakes them.

name: Attention mechanism (Bahdanau, Cho and Bengio)
title: Learning where to look
organization: Bahdanau, Cho & Bengio · Université de Montréal
summary: Bahdanau, Cho and Bengio's RNNsearch weights all source words afresh for each output word, not one fixed vector.
impact: Soft attention spreads to captioning, speech and production translation, then becomes the Transformer's core.

name: Sequence-to-sequence learning
title: One sequence becomes another
summary: Sutskever, Vinyals and Le's LSTM ensemble out-translates a phrase-based system, 34.81 to 33.30 BLEU.
impact: The encoder-decoder becomes a reusable interface, from image captions to the Transformer.

name: Adam optimizer
title: Adam changes the training toolkit
summary: Kingma and Ba's Adam gives every parameter its own step size from bias-corrected gradient moment estimates.
impact: Adam and its AdamW variant become the standard optimizer for Transformers and large language models.

name: ResNet
title: Depth without the degradation
summary: Microsoft's He, Zhang, Ren and Sun train 152-layer residual networks and win ImageNet 2015 at 3.57% top-5 error.
impact: Skip connections become a default, wrapping every Transformer sub-layer that language models inherit.

name: OpenAI
title: OpenAI is founded
summary: Altman, Musk, Brockman and Sutskever launch OpenAI, a nonprofit AI lab with $1 billion in pledged funding.
impact: A funded nonprofit rival draws talent from corporate labs and makes AGI governance a mainstream question.

name: AlphaGo vs Lee Sedol
title: Move 37. A new kind of intuition.
summary: DeepMind's AlphaGo beats Lee Sedol 4 to 1 at Go in Seoul, with the startling Move 37 in game two.
impact: Learned evaluation plus search cracks Go and launches the AlphaGo Zero, AlphaZero and MuZero line.

name: Google Neural Machine Translation
title: Phrase tables give way to neural networks
summary: Google moves all Chinese to English in Translate, about 18 million translations a day, to a deep LSTM network.
impact: Translate goes neural for 16 directions by November, and its wordpieces pass to the Transformer and BERT.

name: Transformer
title: Attention is all you need
summary: Eight researchers unveil the Transformer, an attention-only model scoring 28.4 BLEU on English-German translation.
impact: Its attention-only design becomes the base of BERT, T5, GPT-3 and the Vision Transformer.

name: Deep reinforcement learning from human preferences (RLHF)
title: A reward learned from human choices
summary: OpenAI and DeepMind agents learn from rewards fit to human clip comparisons, a backflip from 900 judgments.
impact: Reward models fit to human comparisons become RLHF, the tuning step behind InstructGPT and ChatGPT.

name: AlphaZero
title: Mastery through self-play
summary: One DeepMind algorithm learns chess, shogi and Go from the rules alone and beats the top program in each.
impact: A single self-play recipe displaces three hand-built engine traditions and seeds MuZero and AlphaTensor.

name: GPT-1
title: The first GPT
summary: OpenAI pretrains a Transformer decoder on 7,000 books, then fine-tunes it to records on 9 of 12 language tasks.
impact: Pretrain on raw text, then adapt becomes the recipe that GPT-2 and GPT-3 scale up.

name: BERT
title: BERT reads both ways
summary: Google's BERT learns by predicting masked words from both sides, setting records on 11 language tasks.
impact: Within a year Google applies it to about 1 in 10 US English searches, and RoBERTa and DistilBERT build on it.

name: GPT-2
title: GPT-2 and the release debate
summary: OpenAI announces GPT-2, a 1.5 billion parameter language model, but withholds its full weights over misuse risk.
impact: Its prompt-as-task recipe scales into GPT-3, and staged release becomes a lasting term in launch policy.

name: T5
title: Every language task is text-to-text
summary: Google's T5 frames every language task as text in, text out, and releases the 750 GB C4 corpus with its models.
impact: The text-to-text format and C4 become reused defaults, underpinning mT5, T0, UL2 and Flan-T5.

name: Scaling laws for neural language models
title: Bigger models, predictably better
summary: Kaplan's OpenAI team finds language-model loss falls as power laws in parameters, data and compute.
impact: Labs start sizing models by extrapolation; GPT-3 follows its big-model advice until Chinchilla revises it.

name: GPT-3
title: GPT-3 scales up
summary: OpenAI's 175 billion parameter GPT-3 performs many language tasks from a few examples in its prompt.
impact: Prompting one hosted model becomes an alternative to per-task fine-tuning, and metered API access a template.

name: DDPM
title: Learning to reverse noise
summary: Berkeley's Ho, Jain and Abbeel train an image model to reverse noise, reaching a record 3.17 FID on CIFAR-10.
impact: Diffusion becomes competitive with GANs, leading to guidance, latent diffusion and Stable Diffusion.

name: Waymo fully driverless public service
title: The driver's seat goes empty
summary: Waymo opens rides with no one behind the wheel to Waymo One riders across about 50 square miles of metro Phoenix.
impact: Paid public robotaxi rides without a safety driver begin, growing to over 400,000 rides a week by 2026.

name: Vision Transformer
title: Images become patch sequences
summary: Dosovitskiy's Google team runs a plain Transformer on 16x16 image patches and reaches 88.55% on ImageNet.
impact: Images and text come to share one architecture, the base for Swin, DINO, MAE and CLIP's image encoder.

name: AlphaFold 2
title: A 50-year biology problem
summary: DeepMind's AlphaFold 2 predicts unseen protein structures at CASP14 with a median score of 92.4 GDT.
impact: Blind structure prediction nears lab accuracy, and over 200 million predicted structures are public by 2022.

name: DALL·E
title: DALL·E: language becomes image
summary: OpenAI's DALL·E, a 12-billion-parameter transformer, draws images from captions such as an avocado armchair.
impact: A typed sentence becomes the control for image generation, though diffusion replaces its method by 2022.

name: GitHub Copilot
title: Your AI pair programmer
summary: GitHub previews Copilot, an editor extension in which OpenAI's Codex suggests whole lines and functions.
impact: Code generation becomes a daily paid tool, and its security and licensing questions turn concrete.

name: Latent diffusion models
title: Diffusion leaves pixel space
summary: Rombach's Munich team runs image diffusion in an autoencoder's compressed latent space, not raw pixels.
impact: Diffusion gets cheap enough to release openly: the design ships as Stable Diffusion in 2022.

name: InstructGPT
title: Learning what users prefer
summary: Labelers prefer OpenAI's 1.3-billion-parameter InstructGPT, tuned on human feedback, to 175-billion GPT-3.
impact: Preference tuning becomes the standard post-training stage, and ChatGPT applies it to dialogue.

name: Chinchilla scaling laws
title: Scale the data, not just the model
summary: DeepMind's 70B Chinchilla, trained on 1.4 trillion tokens, beats the 280B Gopher at equal compute.
impact: Training data comes to scale with model size, near 20 tokens per parameter, paving the way for LLaMA.

name: DALL·E 2
title: DALL·E 2
summary: OpenAI's DALL·E 2 generates and edits 1024x1024 images by decoding CLIP embeddings with diffusion.
impact: Text-to-image becomes an editing tool for non-specialists, and its gated rollout frames the openness debate.

name: Stable Diffusion
title: Stable Diffusion opens up
summary: Stability AI releases Stable Diffusion with downloadable weights that run on a consumer GPU.
impact: An open checkpoint becomes a substrate: DreamBooth, ControlNet and community fine-tunes follow within months.

name: ChatGPT release
title: Hello, ChatGPT.
summary: OpenAI releases ChatGPT, a free preview of a GPT-3.5 model tuned with human feedback to hold a dialogue.
impact: An estimated 100 million monthly users by January 2023 made chat the default way to use language models.

name: LLaMA
title: LLaMA enters the picture
summary: Meta releases LLaMA, 7B to 65B models trained on public data; LLaMA-13B beats 175B GPT-3 on most benchmarks.
impact: Leaked weights, Alpaca, Vicuna and llama.cpp moved competitive language models onto single GPUs and laptops.

name: GPT-4
title: GPT-4 raises the bar
summary: OpenAI launches GPT-4, accepting images and text, scoring 86.4% on MMLU and passing a simulated bar exam.
impact: It became the yardstick rivals were measured against and set a norm of withholding size, data and compute.

name: Claude release
title: Meet Claude
summary: Anthropic releases Claude and Claude Instant via API and partners, trained with Constitutional AI.
impact: It gave buyers a credible rival to ChatGPT and put AI-feedback alignment into a shipping commercial product.

name: Segment Anything
title: A foundation model for segmentation
summary: Kirillov and Meta colleagues release SAM, which masks objects from a click or box, and 1.1 billion masks.
impact: Apache 2.0 weights made SAM a segmentation primitive for medical, satellite and video tools.

name: Llama 2
title: Llama 2 opens commercial access
summary: Meta releases Llama 2 at 7B, 13B and 70B with chat versions, licensed for commercial use under conditions.
impact: A large share of applied work moved from hosted APIs to self-run weights, seeding thousands of fine-tunes.

name: Mistral 7B
title: A smaller open-weight contender
summary: Mistral AI releases Mistral 7B under Apache 2.0, a 7.3B model that beats Llama 2 13B on all tested benchmarks.
impact: 7B became a default base for self-hosting, and Mistral 7B one of its generation's most fine-tuned models.

name: Bletchley Declaration
title: The Bletchley Declaration
summary: 28 countries and the EU, including the US and China, sign a non-binding statement on frontier AI risk.
impact: It launched a summit series, a Bengio-chaired science report and national AI safety institutes.

name: Google Gemini
title: The Gemini era begins
summary: Google DeepMind unveils Gemini 1.0 in Ultra, Pro and Nano sizes, trained on text, images, audio and video.
impact: Google rebuilt Bard, its API and Pixel features around one model family; Bard itself became Gemini.

name: OpenAI Sora
title: Sora imagines in motion
summary: OpenAI previews Sora, a text-to-video model that renders coherent clips up to a minute long from prompts.
impact: It reset the bar for generated video; Veo, Movie Gen and CogVideoX followed within 8 months.

name: Claude 3
title: Claude 3 arrives
summary: Anthropic releases Opus, Sonnet and Haiku as one Claude 3 family, with image input and a 200,000-token window.
impact: Shipping a priced range of tiers, not one model, became a standard way to offer frontier models.

name: AlphaFold 3
title: AlphaFold 3 expands the picture
summary: AlphaFold 3 predicts the joint 3D structure of proteins bound to DNA, RNA, small-molecule ligands and ions.
impact: One model replaced a patchwork of docking and nucleic-acid tools, and open copies like Boltz-1 followed.

name: GPT-4o
title: GPT-4o: a more natural interface
summary: OpenAI's GPT-4o handles text, images and audio in one model, answering speech in as little as 232 milliseconds.
impact: Real-time voice and vision became the expected shape of a frontier assistant, then a developer API.

name: Claude 3.5 Sonnet
title: Claude 3.5 Sonnet
summary: Anthropic's mid-tier Claude 3.5 Sonnet outscores Claude 3 Opus at twice its speed, and previews Artifacts.
impact: Flagship capability at workhorse prices made it a default backend for coding tools and agents.

name: Llama 3.1
title: A frontier-scale downloadable model
summary: Meta releases downloadable Llama 3.1 weights, led by a dense 405B model with a 128,000-token context window.
impact: Near-frontier quality became something a team could host itself, resetting the open-weight bar.

name: EU AI Act
title: The EU AI Act enters into force
summary: The EU AI Act, Regulation 2024/1689, enters into force, starting a phased clock for its obligations.
impact: A major jurisdiction turned AI principles into binding law, with fines up to 7% of global turnover.

name: OpenAI o1
title: Thinking before answering
summary: OpenAI previews o1, a model trained with reinforcement learning to reason at length before it answers.
impact: Inference-time compute became a second scaling axis, and DeepSeek-R1 and others followed.

name: Hopfield and Hinton Nobel Prize
title: Neural networks win a Nobel
summary: Hopfield and Hinton win the Physics Nobel for the 1982 Hopfield network and the 1985 Boltzmann machine.
impact: Physics' top prize declared 1980s neural-network research foundational to modern AI.

name: AlphaFold Nobel Prize
title: AI meets the Nobel in Chemistry
summary: Baker wins half the chemistry Nobel for protein design; Hassabis and Jumper share half for AlphaFold.
impact: The Nobel record now counts a machine-learned predictor and computer-designed proteins as chemistry.

name: Claude computer use
title: Claude uses a computer
summary: Anthropic's public beta lets Claude 3.5 Sonnet drive a desktop from screenshots, scoring 14.9% on OSWorld.
impact: GUI agents became a documented API tool; OpenAI and Google shipped their own within months.

name: Model Context Protocol
title: A common language for tools
summary: Anthropic opens the Model Context Protocol, a JSON-RPC standard linking AI apps to tools and data.
impact: OpenAI, VS Code, Cursor and Zed adopted it, making one lab's spec the shared layer for AI tool access.

name: DeepSeek-R1
title: DeepSeek-R1 opens reasoning
summary: DeepSeek releases R1 under the MIT License, a downloadable reasoning model it reports as on par with o1.
impact: Its RL recipe was cheap enough to replicate within weeks, and its distilled models became open baselines.

name: Claude Code
title: Claude Code enters the terminal
summary: Anthropic previews Claude Code, a terminal agent that edits files, runs tests and commits, with Claude 3.7 Sonnet.
impact: Coding help shifted from suggesting lines to an agent that runs the edit, test and fix loop itself.

name: Gemini 2.5
title: Gemini makes thinking explicit
summary: Google DeepMind releases Gemini 2.5 Pro Experimental, a thinking model that debuts at the top of LMArena.
impact: Google folded reasoning into its multimodal flagship, helping make thinking a 2025 industry default.

name: Qwen3
title: Qwen 3 broadens open reasoning
summary: Alibaba's Qwen team releases Qwen3 under Apache 2.0: 8 models from 0.6B to 235B, each with a thinking switch.
impact: Open reasoning became deployable from phone to server, with thinking a per-request dial, not a second model.

name: AlphaEvolve
title: Breeding algorithms with a language model
summary: DeepMind's AlphaEvolve evolves code with Gemini and multiplies 4x4 complex matrices with 48 products, not 49.
impact: Evolving code against an automatic score becomes a reusable discovery method, copied in open source within months.

name: Claude 4
title: Claude 4 gets to work
summary: Anthropic launches Claude Opus 4 and Sonnet 4, scoring 72.5% and 72.7% on SWE-bench Verified.
impact: Agentic coding became the organizing purpose of a leading model family, with Opus 4 deployed under ASL-3.

name: Bartz v. Anthropic
title: Fair use for training, not for piracy
summary: Judge Alsup rules training Claude on books was fair use; keeping over 7 million pirated copies was not.
impact: Anthropic then settled for at least $1.5 billion, about $3,100 per work, pricing pirated training data.

name: AI gold at IMO 2025
title: Olympiad gold in natural language
summary: Gemini Deep Think and an OpenAI model score 35 of 42 at IMO 2025 with prose proofs, the gold cut-off.
impact: Olympiad proofs move from hand-formalized Lean and days of search to prose within the exam's 4.5 hours.

name: gpt-oss
title: OpenAI returns to open weights
summary: OpenAI releases gpt-oss-120b and gpt-oss-20b under Apache 2.0, its first open-weight language models since GPT-2.
impact: A reasoning model near o4-mini level now runs on one 80GB GPU, downloadable and outside OpenAI's API.

name: GPT-5
title: GPT-5 arrives
summary: OpenAI makes GPT-5, a router choosing between fast and reasoning models, the default for all ChatGPT users.
impact: Test-time reasoning becomes the default for ChatGPT's mass audience rather than a model users had to pick.

name: California SB 53 (Transparency in Frontier AI Act)
title: Disclosure in place of a kill switch
summary: Newsom signs SB 53, making the largest frontier AI developers publish safety frameworks and report incidents.
impact: New York rebuilt its RAISE Act on SB 53 in 2026, while the White House urged Congress to preempt such laws.

name: Gemini 3
title: Gemini 3
summary: Google releases Gemini 3 Pro and puts it into Search's AI Mode on day one, reporting 1501 Elo on LMArena.
impact: A new frontier model reaches Google Search at launch rather than after months of separate testing.

name: Pentagon designates Anthropic a supply-chain risk
title: Red lines labeled a supply-chain risk
summary: Hegseth moves to label Anthropic a supply-chain risk over two limits on Claude's military use.
impact: One court voids it as retaliation; the D.C. Circuit upholds a second, 2 to 1.

name: Claude Mythos Preview
title: The model Anthropic held back
summary: Anthropic withholds Claude Mythos Preview over its exploit skill and lends it only to vetted defenders.
impact: Release becomes sequenced by capability: defenders first, filtered public access 9 weeks later.

name: Erdős unit distance disproof
title: Erdős's grid is finally beaten
summary: An unnamed OpenAI model disproves Erdős's 1946 unit distance conjecture with number-field point sets.
impact: Gowers would back it for the Annals, and within a week it inspired another Erdős disproof.

name: OpenAI Hugging Face incident
title: The evaluation that escaped its sandbox
summary: OpenAI names its own models, testing on ExploitGym, as the agents that broke into Hugging Face.
impact: Evaluation containment turns public: OpenAI pauses deployment RL runs and Hawley opens an inquiry.

name: AI Act enforcement
title: AI Act enforcement expands
summary: EU AI Act transparency rules take effect: chatbots must say they are AI and AI output must be marked.
impact: Labeling duties gain fines of up to €15 million or 3% of turnover, while high-risk rules slip to 2027.

name: GPT-6 Astra
title: Astra: the next frontier
summary: OpenAI releases GPT-6 Astra, the first model to cross its own Critical cybersecurity threshold.
impact: A lab ships past its own severe-risk line, gating offensive cyber use and monitoring all tool use.

name: OpenAI's Navier-Stokes blow-up claim
title: A claimed blowup for the fluid equations
summary: OpenAI says some 10,000 agents running an unreleased model proved forced Navier-Stokes blowup, checked in Lean.
impact: Clay calls the problem apparently settled yet lists it as open; experts dispute the Lean match and the credit.

name: Thomson Reuters v. ROSS Intelligence (Third Circuit)
title: No fair use for training a Westlaw rival
organization: U.S. Court of Appeals for the Third Circuit
summary: The Third Circuit holds that copying 2,243 Westlaw headnotes to train ROSS's legal search AI is not fair use.
impact: The first appellate ruling on AI training recognizes a training-data market but sets generative models aside.

name: OpenAI's quasi-Riemann hypothesis proof
title: A claimed fence around zeta's zeros
summary: OpenAI posts 722 AI-written papers claiming a quasi-Riemann hypothesis and no Siegel zeros.
impact: Banks, Kerr and Green rework the Siegel proof in two weeks; Sarnak withholds the word theorem.

name: Exponential Time Hypothesis refutation
title: Two labs claim 3-SAT escapes exponential time
summary: OpenAI and Anthropic models independently claim Lean-checked 2^o(n) algorithms for 3-SAT, refuting ETH.
impact: ETH's own authors open a review they say is not certification; simplified proofs appear within days.
